IncidentBot: [ALERT] High throttle_event rate on rwd-prod-autoscale (policy=autoscale-pool-1) — paging oncall. link: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/12345 :rotating_light:
Maria (SRE): I'm paged, looking now. grabbing latest metrics from the dashboard.
Raj Patel: I'm jumping in too. quick check: queue_depth spike on gpu-pool-1 at ~t0+30s, tokens/sec jumped 3x, throttle_events went up immediately after.
Maria (SRE): seeing the same. errors are 503s for a small subset of customers hitting heavy batching paths.
Sam K: do we have an ongoing deploy?
Elaine C: No deploys in last 30m per deploy-bot.
Raj Patel: tailing gateway logs:
```
kubectl -n prod logs deploy/gateway -f --since=10m | grep throttle
2026-03-05T14:11:02Z gateway ERROR throttle event model=fast-embed pool=gpu-pool-1 queue_depth=64 tokens=12000
2026-03-05T14:11:05Z gateway WARN backlog growing: queue_depth=72
```
Maria (SRE): looks like prefix cache misses + sudden traffic pattern = overloaded batch formation. autoscaler didn't react fast enough because scaling policy uses 60s window.
Raj Patel: I can trigger a manual scale to add 2 nodes to gpu-pool-1 to relieve pressure. Do we want that while we root cause?
Sam K: yes, manual scale now. I'll also open a temporary fallback route to a cheaper-but-compatible model to shed load for affected customers.
Maria (SRE): doing manual scale: `rwdctl pools scale gpu-pool-1 --add 2 --reason \"emergency throttle spike\"`
oncall-rotation-bot: @Maria (SRE) manually scaled gpu-pool-1 +2 (request id r-78a3).
Elaine C: adding a quick mute on the throttle_events alert because it's firing noisy duplicate alerts while we mitigate (will add a 10m silence).
Raj Patel: note — muting alert for now is fine, but we should not lose signal. we need a composite alert that only pages when throttle_events > 50 AND queue_depth > 50 for > 30s.
Sam K: agreed. current alert triggers on max single-sample throttle_events > 20 which is too sensitive during traffic spikes. we should change to a rolling average or increase threshold.
Maria (SRE): creating a dashboard panel request: tokens/sec per model, queue_depth heatmap per pool, throttle_events per customer-id. Sam can you take the dashboard PR?
Sam K: yup, I'll create the Grafana panel and a templated dashboard: `rwd-grafana/dashboards/autoscale/pool-1.json`
Raj Patel: runtime team, please confirm whether kernel scheduling or KV cache evictions could amplify latency for longer sequences — can that create sudden tokens/sec bursts? @Runtime Team
Runtime Team: we saw a kernel fallback on pool-1 at 14:10:59 that caused per-token latency to jump ~80ms for some models, which increased in-flight tokens and contributed to queueing. investigating scheduling constraints.
Maria (SRE): mitigation status: manual scale done, fallback route to model-b-lite enabled, error rate dropping.
oncall-rotation-bot: Handoff reminder — Maria (SRE) handing to night oncall Sam K in 25m.
Sam K: I'll take the handoff once stable. next steps in thread.
Elaine C: postmortem / action items we should track: 1) tune alerting rule to composite (owner: Elaine) 2) add queue_depth smoothing + use p95 tokens/sec window (owner: Raj) 3) dashboard for per-model tokens (owner: Sam) 4) autoscaler policy tweak: consider faster scale-up (owner: Runtime Team) 5) update runbook with step to enable fallback route (owner: Maria).
Raj Patel: for (2) proposal: change alert expression from `max(throttle_events) > 20` to `avg_over_time(throttle_events[30s]) > 40 OR (queue_depth > 50 AND avg_over_time(tokens_per_sec[30s]) > 2000)`. this should reduce spurious pages while keeping sensitivity for sustained incidents.
Maria (SRE): also recommend adding suppressions for known maintenance windows and marking deploy tags so alerts won't trigger on deploy-caused queues.
Sam K: I'll open the dashboard PR now and include example panels and a runbook link.
Elaine C: I'll open the alert rule PR with the composite rule and add automated test cases in the alert repo.
Runtime Team: we'll prototype autoscaler fast-path: if queue_depth > 60 for >15s, spawn a burst pod immediately (owner: Runtime Team).
Maria (SRE): can we add a short-term tweak to the autoscaler to use tokens_in_flight metric? (that would more directly correlate with throttle risk)
Runtime Team: good idea — we'll prototype it and run a canary on a small pool.
Raj Patel: follow-up load test: reproduce pattern with synthetic traffic that ramps tokens/sec 3x over 30s and check autoscaler reaction. Raj -> I'll run it tomorrow 09:00 UTC and post results.
Sam K: noted. I'll update the oncall playbook with the new composite alert snippet and the dashboard URL once PR merges.
Maria (SRE): summary: incident mitigated by manual scale + fallback routing; muted noisy alert temporarily; action items assigned. I'll mark this thread for postmortem and link to the incident doc.
IncidentBot: incident 2026-03-05T14:11 #INC-315 closed (root cause: autoscaler scale-up latency + kernel fallback causing token burst) :white_check_mark:
Sam K: handing over to night oncall, leaving notes in pagerduty and incident doc. good job team. :thumbsup:
Elaine C: filing follow-up tickets now.
Raj Patel: adding test scenarios to evg-load repo.
Maria (SRE): thanks everyone — will follow up with PM on customer impact (a subset of customers had transient 503s for ~3-7 minutes).
Sam K: acknowledged.
